clue.text: Efficient, as fish and chips should be?

definitions.meaning: someone efficient earns their pay and is good at the job

definitions.text: as fish and chips should be?
definitions.meaning: fish and chips are traditionally sprinkled with salt, so they should be worth (deserving of) their salt

explanation.surface: A remark that an efficient chip shop's fish supper should be properly seasoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a competent person is read literally: fish and chips, a British takeaway dish, deserve their salt.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who deserves their wages, i.e. a capable worker.

clue.text: Argument over vessel in service

indicators.note: in a down clue over signals turning the word upward, read backwards

parts.note: a row is an argument
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A quarrel on board a ship during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship is a religious service.

clue.text: Deny being concerned with the dessert I had

parts.note: re means about, concerning
pud is British slang for pudding, dessert
to have a meal is to eat, so had gives ate

explanation.surface: Someone denying they ate the pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or disown, to deny.

clue.text: With it, flier becomes a 'thick-skinned creature

parts.note: hip means fashionable, with it
PO is a Pilot Officer in the RAF, a flier

explanation.surface: A suggestion that adding something turns a bird into a hippo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a bird, but it is an airman: PO is the RAF rank Pilot Officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is known for its very thick hide.

clue.text: Norwegian navy seen around the Arctic

indicators.note: the two outer pieces are seen surrounding the middle word

parts.note: Nor is the abbreviation for Norwegian
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Norway's fleet spotted in polar waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norwegian' and 'navy' read as one phrase, a fleet, but they are two pieces split apart by 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic regions lie in the far north.

clue.text: Gregarious agents having a place in the sun

indicators.note: the agents are given a place inside the word for the sun

parts.note: Sol is the sun
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, its agents

explanation.surface: Sociable spies with a holiday home in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A social person enjoys company, as a gregarious one does.

clue.text: How a crowd startled lonely poet suddenly

definitions.text: How a crowd startled lonely poet
definitions.meaning: Wordsworth, wandering lonely as a cloud, came on a crowd of daffodils without warning

explanation.surface: A poet alone is surprised by a throng appearing without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The lines are Wordsworth's: 'When all at once I saw a crowd, / A host, of golden daffodils'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means abruptly or simultaneously, i.e. without warning.

clue.text: Subject to official provisos, it covers leaders

indicators.note: the leading letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: A document saying it covers its leading figures, subject to official conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' reads as a phrase, but 'Subject' is the definition and 'to' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject for discussion.

clue.text: Convincing businessman

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A persuasive businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: One printed word does the work of two pieces: 'business' and 'man' are read separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is persuasive and compelling.

clue.text: Either way, one has to decorate again

indicators.note: the word reads the same whichever direction you take it, so the whole answer is its own wordplay

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone saying one must redecorate whichever way things go.
explanation.definitionFit: To put fresh wallpaper up is to decorate a room once more.

clue.text: Nymph improvised song

definitions.meaning: The sea nymph who kept Odysseus on her island
a Caribbean song form, often with topical lyrics made up on the spot

explanation.surface: A nymph extemporising a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: One name serves both the Homeric sea nymph and the West Indian song style known for improvised verses.

clue.text: Old-fashioned hotel created by waterfall

definitions.meaning: a dated British word for a spa hotel offering water cures
... power is electricity generated by falling water

explanation.surface: A quaint hotel built beside a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a hydro was a Victorian-style spa hotel; the second sense is the electricity short form.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spa hotel of the old school and power produced by falling water.

clue.text: Listen to walrus, perhaps, suffering

parts.note: to listen to is to hear
a walrus is a style of drooping moustache, and tache is the informal short form

explanation.surface: Hearing a walrus bellow in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walrus' suggests the animal, but here it is a walrus moustache, colloquially a tache.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional anguish or grief is a kind of suffering.

clue.text: Sole policy

definitions.meaning: a ... sole is a thick raised sole on a shoe
a party's ... is its declared set of policies

explanation.surface: A single policy being announced.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a thick shoe sole and a party's published programme.

clue.text: Anticipate a lot of trees to both sides

parts.note: a forest is a large area of trees
something given to both sides goes to all parties

explanation.surface: Foreseeing woodland lining both edges of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act first and prevent something, anticipating it.

clue.text: Throw out of Security Council position

parts.note: the Security Council is an organ of the United Nations, abbreviated UN
a seat is a position, as on a committee

explanation.surface: Expelling a member from their place on the Security Council.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat someone is to remove them from office or from a saddle.

clue.text: I can purée bananas for gourmet

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A cook offering to purée bananas for a food lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the fruit being puréed but means mad, rearranging I CAN PUREE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure, one devoted to fine food, is a gourmet.

clue.text: Unsophisticated detective's reported witticism

indicators.note: the detective's name is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes is the fictional detective
a pun is a witticism

explanation.surface: A rustic joke attributed to a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' signals that HOLMES is spoken, giving HOMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and simple, lacking sophistication.

clue.text: Reluctant to admit blunder making wine

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so the word for blunder goes inside the word for reluctant

parts.note: reluctant can mean shy, hesitant
to blunder is to err

explanation.surface: Someone too proud to confess a mistake made while producing wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain.

clue.text: Dispose of piece of furniture

definitions.meaning: to resolve or deal with a matter

explanation.surface: Getting rid of an item of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to deal with a matter finally and a long wooden bench with a high back.

clue.text: Error as only 100 is added to 1000

indicators.note: the thousand is joined on after the other pieces

parts.note: sole means only, single
C is the Roman numeral for 100
M is the Roman numeral for 1000

explanation.surface: A complaint that adding 100 to 1000 is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a mistake in grammar or etiquette.

clue.text: A way to cover up a filthy place for propriety

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, covering it

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something
a pigsty is a filthy place

explanation.surface: A method for hiding a squalid spot for decency's sake.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty means decorum and propriety in behaviour or dress.

clue.text: Roderick managed to comp a mile

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Roderick managed to comp a mile'; the scan smudges the word after 'comp' and no search recovers it, so the piece giving DO cannot be confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Roderick managed to comp a mile

clue.text: Develop a clear structure in appropriate military HQ

parts.note: to appropriate is to take for oneself
SHAPE was NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe

explanation.surface: An army headquarters getting properly organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, take. SHAPE is the acronym of NATO's European headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: When a plan takes form it gains a definite shape or organisation.

clue.text: College book

definitions.meaning: A book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A college library volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a famous college and a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Container for drink — squash, for instance

definitions.meaning: a dried hollowed fruit shell used as a flask
squash is one of the plants in the ... family

explanation.surface: A bottle for a drink such as squash, the British fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' tempts as the diluted fruit drink, sold in Britain as a cordial; here it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard-shelled fruit both serves as a vessel and includes squashes as an example.

clue.text: Hopeless person George I put inside

indicators.note: the word for I is put inside George's royal initials

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's cipher
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A king called George is jailed and done for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George I' looks like the first King George, but I is ONE placed in GR.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone beyond help or doomed.

clue.text: Grease coating some cord

indicators.note: one word covers the other, so the word for grease wraps round the word for some

parts.note: lard is pig fat, a grease
any can mean some

explanation.surface: Grease being smeared on a length of cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord, such as one worn round the neck to hold a whistle or pass.

clue.text: These boatmen are ordinary people

definitions.meaning: people propelling flat-bottomed boats with a pole, as on the Cam
in Britain ... are customers or the general public

explanation.surface: A claim that those who pole boats are regular folk.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English punters are everyday customers or gamblers, and also people who pole a punt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both people poling punts and members of the general public.

clue.text: Monday's child — wise man, and prude

parts.note: King Solomon is proverbial for wisdom
Mrs Grundy is a byword for a prudish, censorious person

explanation.surface: A child born on Monday described as wise yet prim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monday's child' suggests the rhyme 'fair of face', but the nursery-rhyme figure born on a Monday is meant. Mrs Grundy, from an 18th-century play, stands for prudishness.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme figure was born on a Monday, so the phrase identifies him.
